turns.explanation:
In this public goods game, I need to balance cooperation and self-interest. The payoff structure means that every unit I contribute returns 0.5 to me (as part of the public return), so I lose 0.5 per unit contributed. However, other players' contributions benefit me fully at 0.5 per unit. This creates an incentive to free-ride—contribute nothing while hoping others contribute.

However, since this is a 6-round repeated game, reputation and reciprocity matter. If I contribute nothing in round 1, others may retaliate by also contributing nothing in future rounds, leading to mutual defection and low earnings for everyone. A moderate contribution signals cooperation and may encourage others to reciprocate, leading to higher mutual returns over time.

Starting with a moderate contribution of 10 (50% of my endowment) balances these concerns: it demonstrates willingness to cooperate, is not so high as to be exploited, and provides a reasonable baseline for potentially cooperative play in subsequent rounds. This should maximize my cumulative earnings better than either pure free-riding or full contribution.
